key_insight: Exposing embodied coding agents to benchmark success criteria can improve verifier scores without improving instruction-faithful task performance or cross-task transfer.
engineering_relevance: Robot-agent evaluation should distinguish gains on exposed verification rules from robust task completion under instruction-consistent criteria.
method: Compare self-improving agents with and without Criteria Exposure (CE).
Re-evaluate programs after slight, instruction-preserving changes to success criteria.
Assess cross-task skill transfer and propose instruction-faithful criteria.
evidence_signal: Controlled experiments show that CE raises success rates under the exposed criteria, but the advantage disappears under slight criteria changes, while learned skills transfer poorly across tasks.
watch_item: The abstract provides no benchmark details or effect sizes, limiting assessment of the findings' scope and magnitude.
paper_title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
